subject: SIG follow-up: clarification on Dedicated GPU separation and noisy-neighbor evidence
messages:

Cc: procurement@acme.com

Subject: SIG follow-up: dedicated GPU tenancy questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending the initial SIG snapshot last week. Acme's security team reviewed the responses and we have a handful of clarifying questions specifically around Dedicated GPU tenancy and noisy-neighbor risk. High level asks below; we need concise answers and any evidence artifacts you can share (traces, diagrams, short configs). We're trying to close the SIG next week.

Top questions:
- Do tenants on Dedicated pools ever share GPU DRAM or device-resident memory pages? If not, how is physical memory isolation enforced?
- How does Redwood manage KV cache per-tenant? Is cache stored in shared process memory, or is it pinned per allocation/tenant?
- Eviction / preemption behavior: what signals are emitted, are there observable latency spikes for remaining tenants? Do you have examples/traces?
- Any known side-channel mitigations (clock jitter, micro-architectural mitigations) applied to dedicated nodes?

Requested artifacts:
- Short diagram of runtime separation (process/container/hypervisor boundaries)
- A sample eviction trace for a controlled preemption event
- A concise statement we can include in SIG about data-in-GPU isolation

I've attached a one-page follow-up (acme_SIG_followup_v1.pdf) with inline comment markers. Let me know if we should route technical artifacts to our security mailbox or the procurement thread.

Best,
John

John,

Thanks — we can provide all of the requested clarifications and a small set of evidence artifacts. Quick answers up front and then a pointer to the attachments below.

Short answers (summary):
- GPU DRAM: tenants never share the same physical GPU DRAM allocation. Dedicated pools allocate devices at the instance level; we use a combination of device assignment and a per-tenant memory partitioning layer in the runtime to ensure there are no cross-tenant device-resident pages.
- KV cache: KV caches are scoped to the serving process for a tenant. On Dedicated nodes we spawn tenant-dedicated worker processes that hold their own KV cache in process memory (no shared global cache).
- Eviction/preemption: we surface preemption as an ordered drain: active connections are signaled and a graceful eviction is attempted; if forced, we log an eviction trace and trigger automatic failover to a warm fallback. Observed latency impact is limited to the evicted tenant; we include a sample controlled eviction trace in the attachments.
- Side-channel mitigations: we apply standard microcode/firmware patches and runtime scheduling policies (CPU pinning, jitter reduction) and avoid co-scheduling untrusted tenants on the same GPU when customer-specified isolation is required.

Attachments included: redwood_kv_cache_boundary_design.pdf (2-page design), svc_isolation_summary.xlsx (summary table by pool). Also attaching a short log excerpt (eviction-trace-sample.log) that shows timing and signals for a controlled eviction. If you need raw perf traces we can provide sanitized perf events on a case-by-case basis.

Next steps: Mina (security) will add a concise language block you can paste into SIG. Aditya and I can also set up a short 30-min call if your team wants a walkthrough of the traces.

Cheers,
Karthik

Hi John,

Following up with the formal language block you can use in the SIG (sized for a concise answer):

"Redwood Dedicated pools provide per-tenant device assignment and runtime-level memory partitioning. Tenant workloads run in tenant-dedicated serving processes bound to the assigned device; there are no shared device-resident pages between tenants on Dedicated nodes. KV caching is scoped per-serving process and is not globally shared. Eviction and preemption are recorded with traceable events and a controlled drain workflow; in practice, eviction impact is limited to the evicted tenant and automatic fallback options are available. For customers requiring additional hard separation, Redwood offers single-tenant device reservations and on-prem/private deployment options."

Evidence we are attaching to support the statement:
- redwood_kv_cache_boundary_design.pdf (diagram and memory partition callouts)
- eviction-trace-sample.log (sanitized trace from a controlled eviction run)
- internal runbook excerpt (we'll surface the runbook section via shared drive link)

Drive link to sanitized trace and runbook excerpt: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cExampleDriveLink
